title: Explicit Counterexample Disproves the 1939 Jacobian Conjecture in Dimensions ≥ 3
whyItMatters: Disproved Ott-Heinrich Keller’s famous 87-year-old Jacobian Conjecture (Smale’s 16th Problem) in dimensions ≥ 3 with a 3-line polynomial map verifiable in seconds via SymPy.
summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge—prompted by a question from Akhil Mathew and collaborating with Claude Fable 5—posted on X an explicit three-variable polynomial map from ℂ³ to ℂ³ whose Jacobian determinant is identically −2, yet maps three distinct points to (−1/4, 0, 0). Because an invertible map cannot merge distinct points, this single compact formula instantaneously refuted the 1939 Jacobian Conjecture for every dimension n ≥ 3.
technicalHighlights: Refuted Keller’s 1939 conjecture (one of Steve Smale’s 18 problems for the 21st century) for all n ≥ 3 with an elementary explicit counterexample.
Checkable by hand or in 10 lines of SymPy / WolframAlpha within seconds of the X post, bypassing multi-month refereeing lag.
Showcased how public frontier models (Claude Fable 5) paired with an expert mathematician can crack century-scale algebra problems in a weekend.
caveats: Leaves the two-dimensional case (n = 2) of the Jacobian Conjecture still open; originally announced informally on X before follow-up arXiv analyses.

scoreRationale.verification: Trivially and universally verified algebraically (determinant = −2, three distinct preimages map to the same point).
